question: In the Li3PO4-coated NCM study, how much did the charge-transfer resistance rise over 50 cycles for the bare and the coated material, and what capacity did each retain after 100 cycles at 1C?
expect: bare 27.99 to 224.04 Ω, coated 14.88 to 144.75 Ω (p8.L38-40); retention 75.4% bare vs 88.4% coated (p8.L34-36)
rendered: According to the text, the charge-transfer resistance (Rct) for the bare NCM material increased from 27.99 to 224.04 Ω during 50 cycles, whereas for the LPO-coated NCM material, it only increased from 14.88 to 144.75 Ω. After 100 cycles, the bare NCM material retained 75.4% of its initial discharge capacity, whereas the LPO-coated NCM material retained 88.4%.
